To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a two-dimensional phononic crystal with a square array of steel tubular inclusions in water can be designed to have a tunable pass band in its stop band and that this pass band can be exploited to construct a frequency selective waveguide.

the transmission spectrum of two dimensional phononic crystals with square array of hollow tubes embedded in a fluid is tunable and that two waveguides made of these crystals with different inner radius can be used to separate two specific frequencies.
the frequency of a tunable narrow pass band in a two-dimensional phononic crystal with a square lattice of hollow steel inclusions is tunable by changing the inner radius of these inclusions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of two dimensional phononic crystals with tunable narrow pass bands.
the development of acoustic band gap structures for elastic wave propagation.
the development of tunable narrow pass band phononic crystals with potential applications to acoustic filters, waveguides, and sensors.

we have shown the existence of a two dimensional phononic crystal with a narrow pass band in a transmission stop band.
we can control and tune the frequency of the transmission band by changing the inner radius of hollow tubes.

we have shown that the use of two-dimensional phononic crystals with a narrow band gap in the transmission spectrum can be employed to construct a waveguide that transmutes a wide-band signal into a two-frequency signal.

we have developed a new class of phononic crystals with tunable pass bands.
a composite medium with a tunable narrow pass band can be used as a waveguide to selectively transmit a frequency of interest from a broad band signal.
the two dimensional phononic crystal with tunable narrow pass band has been demonstrated to be a potential candidate for the design of frequency-selective waveguides.

the narrow pass band of the composite media can be used to create a frequency filter with a sharp pass band and a sharp stop band, and to design waveguides with selective frequency.
two-dimensional phononic crystals can be used to construct waveguides with narrow band transmission properties.
